Subject: Migration options & recommended next steps — NimbusHealth

Alex / Kelly,

Thanks again for the time earlier. Attached is the initial proposal (PDF) plus a short cost-comparison sheet. High level — there are two pragmatic paths we recommend for Nimbus based on the usage profile you shared:

- Option 1 (Modularize): Per-feature entitlements + metered throughput. Enables you to turn features on per team and avoid upfront reserved commit. Good if you want fine-grained control for pilot teams.
- Option 2 (Throughput-first Reserved): Reserved Dedicated capacity (monthly commit) with feature toggles on top. Better unit economics and latency guarantees for high-volume workloads.

Key asks for you to decide:
1) Do you prefer predictable latency/unit-cost (Option 2) or per-team feature controls with lower initial commitment (Option 1)?
2) Procurement timeline — are you aiming for a Sept/Oct contract signature or a Q4 launch?

A few notes on discounts and credits: we can anchor a 12% introductory discount on a 12-month reserved commit, or a blended 8% on a 6-month commit. We can also offer one-time "quantization credits" to offset initial model tuning if you elect Option 2 and choose 8-bit quantized variants (helps keep costs down). Details in the attached sheet.

Next step: if helpful I can run a short 45-minute workshop with Priya to map your teams to the modular entitlements or to size Dedicated pools. Can do slot options next week.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra

Team — forwarding Alex's questions. Draft answers below so we can finalize the one-pager for Nimbus procurement (requested deadline 2027-09-24):

1) Migration friction (Modular -> Reserved):
- We support smooth rollups: modular entitlements are mapped to seat/role groups in our Console; when you elect to reserve, we convert the historical usage and apply a credit for unused metered spend during the billing period (prorated). There is a one-time mapping exercise (~2-4 hours of solutions time) to align entitlements to Dedicated pools.
- Risks: feature flags with per-team entitlements need manual reconciliation; we suggest a short audit runbook during cutover.

2) Quantization credits and fidelity: 
- The credits are a dollar credit applied to model tuning / validation effort tied to our Redwood Optimize recommendations. They are model-agnostic but intended for customers who adopt lower-precision variants (8-bit/4-bit).
- For your internally tuned models we recommend a fidelity validation step (Priya's team can run a 2-day eval on a subset) — credits cover the evaluation compute and a short tuning pass. If the model requires bespoke precision handling we can keep the full-precision variant on Dedicated and only quantize experimental workloads.

3) Pricing math (quick):
- Example (month): Option 1: metered @ $0.0025/token + feature entitlements $X per seat. Option 2: reserved 1x GPU pool = effective $0.0018/token after 12% anchor discount on 12mo commit; + optional seats for admin features.

Action items (internal): Priya — can you produce the 1-page decision checklist + a short table that maps teams -> recommended path (pilot v scale)? Ben — can you draft the 12mo and 6mo committed numbers (blended) for the sample usage in the spreadsheet? I want these finalized by EOD 9/20 so I can circulate.

Rishi
